review_scope: Static inspection of the test-only mock response gate and retained-backing tests; independent exact-byte forward/reverse reconstruction.
result: no static blocker found in reviewed scope
checks: Both input files match v8 fixed-inputs hashes; the patch and gzip expand to the pinned bytes.
Fresh forward and reverse git apply operations reproduce both files byte for byte.
The mock takes the gate while holding the state mutex and drops the guard before sending the entered signal or awaiting release.
Dropping an unconsumed handle clears only its own token; dropping a consumed handle releases its waiting reply without clearing a newer armed token.
The new gate test arms a second gate before dropping the consumed first handle and checks that the second response stays held.
The existing 2 s admission and 10 s flush bounds and reservation assertions remain in force.
Ordinary timeout/error paths retain the JoinHandle, drop/release the gate, then abort and await the sender; panic/test-future cancellation can only request abort in Drop.
The zero-duration setter disables the reply timer; the test resets an earlier 15 s delay and requires prompt responses.
limitations: No Cargo build, native Rust execution, Clippy, or performance test was run.
The cause of the previously observed timeout is not proven, and queue algorithmic costs remain open.
Async task abort on panic or parent-future cancellation is not itself a joined cleanup.
This review does not qualify the wider client candidate or production release.
